comparison.objective: Candidate tunes and locks a shock absorber to produce safe repeatable stops; board-TK-LWANXU positions two mirrors to route a laser to a detector under beam-blocking rules.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate requires recessed tool insertion, collar fine-adjustment, counterholding, locking, and iterative impact evaluation. The laser task requires bimanual mirror transport, precise pose/orientation alignment, beam-block placement, and safe release.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate requires two non-bottoming dynamic cycles within energy, velocity, and stroke limits and a setting-retention test. The laser task requires two reflections ending within 10 mm of the detector center, no lit-mirror movement, no stray beam, stable objects, and both grippers released. Candidate rubric lacks numeric rebound, overload, collar-drift, and locking-torque limits.
comparison.reason: Both use iterative physical adjustment informed by an observed outcome, but optical path alignment with hazard blocking is a meaningfully different tested ability from force-controlled damper tuning and mechanical locking.
